subject: Edge finishing and assembly quality
hook: Flat panels or built carcasses: which saves you more time?
ig:
Flat panels or built carcasses: which saves you more time? It depends on the job, the van and the site.

A: Cut and edged panels
They stack flat, so one trip can carry a whole kitchen. You assemble in your own way, at your own pace. But that's hours on site or in the unit, often in someone's dining room.

B: Assembled carcasses
They arrive built and checked for square. Site time goes on fitting, not building. But a load of tall units takes up a lot of van, which can mean extra trips on bigger jobs.

Many fitters split it: tall and drawer units assembled in the workshop, simple base and wall units as cut and edged panels.

Fitters and joiners: which way do you work, and why? Comment A, B or SPLIT with the reason. It helps us plan the services that are most useful to you.
fb:
A question for local fitters and joiners: when you order panels, do you prefer them flat or built?

Cut and edged panels pack tight, so you get more in the van, and you stay in control of assembly. Assembled carcasses turn up ready to fit and save site time, but take up far more room.

Lots of people mix it, having tall and drawer units built in the workshop and doing the simple ones themselves.

How do you like to work? Let us know below. We offer both from our Hanley workshop.
